headers.//: HTML pages always revalidate — never serve a stale shell that points at old assets. All marketing pages are at the root, so *.html (not **/*.html, whose **/ wants a directory and skips root index.html).

Vanilla scene scripts have STABLE (unhashed) URLs, so they must revalidate on every load or a bug fix can sit behind a day-old cache. Vite's own bundle (main-<hash>.js / *.css) is content-hashed and safe to cache long.

hosting.//: The React SPA. Every path must serve index.html so TanStack Router owns routing; the hashed Vite bundle is immutable, so it caches hard while the shell revalidates.

headers.//: Catch-all: every non-asset path serves the SPA shell (via the rewrite), and a cached shell points at asset hashes that no longer exist after a deploy.
Re-asserted AFTER the catch-all so it wins for the content-hashed bundle, whose filename changes whenever its content does.
